correctness.rationale: The signed path body has the nonnegative chain polytope as every orthant section and independent uniform coordinate signs. Its covariance is diagonal and its diagonal entries have exact rational integrals from a recursively integrated path transfer. The cosine eigenfunctions of Tf(x)=integral_0^(1-x)f(y)dy have signed eigenvalues (-1)^k 2/((2k+1)pi), and the orthogonal spectral remainder is norm O(3^(-r)). The product-to-sum integral gives an absolutely convergent alternating boundary variance series. Alternating-series bounds prove v1 globally largest and v2 globally smallest among all limiting boundary modes. Uniform remainder estimates control all bulk indices, giving the exact limiting eigenvalue ratio. Exact rational tests through n=26 and numerical convergence checks were run from the embedded checker. Tests supplement, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2019 original provides the unconditional perfect-graph objects. Marchal 2012 provides a closely related trigonometric Markov kernel and a rejection-rate constant numerically equal to our first-end second moment; neither that antecedent nor the coincidence is claimed as original. Shonkwiler--Theis 2026 fully treats the identical positive-orthant chain constraints and gives the bulk one-coordinate density and first moments, but not the all-index boundary second-moment profile, its strict alternating inequalities, or the sharp Euclidean covariance conditioning of the signed family. The nearest published path stable-set facet calculation weights boundary area rather than uniform interior volume. Broad unindexed/implicit coverage remains a stated risk.

value.rationale: The canonical lattice-polytope family is geometrically natural from the classification of unconditional reflexive bodies. Coordinate-uniform Euclidean covariance tests quantitative roundness and is not forced by graph combinatorics or vertex counts. An entire infinite-dimensional sequence has only O(1) exceptional endpoint modes, but those modes keep a sharp non-unit global condition number; the alternating boundary law identifies the exceptional directions and supplies nontrivial exact constants and proof. This is stronger than a routine computation of the already-known marginal bulk density.
